fact_text: 8oz is a Karachi burger and restaurant brand that began as a delivery and takeaway concept after COVID, but its first shop ended up with a small dining room that became the main format.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The first 8oz outlet was a commercial space of about 1,000 square feet in Bukhari Commercial, Karachi, with the store on the ground floor and the kitchen upstairs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said the original Bukhari branch was a small restaurant with 18 seats.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: At the interview date of 30 Jan 2026 the founders said the brand can seat up to 90 people at one time across its outlets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders first looked at shops of 300 to 400 square feet, which was too small for the planned format, before taking the larger Bukhari space.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said the brand's early fame came from a bone marrow burger, which puzzled some customers who asked how bone marrow could go with a burger.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The 8oz menu goes well beyond burgers to steaks, pastas, sandwiches, salads and soups, and the founders said it has more than 100 items.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said the restaurant carries more than 200 items at ingredient level, which makes controlling theft and accountability hard for the operation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The 8oz patty is about 226 grams, which the founders said matches the international standard 8-ounce patty size; the name 8oz was chosen to set that expectation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said most Pakistani burger outlets served patties of only 80 to 110 grams, which they saw as the market gap for a larger patty that leaves a normal person full.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: Besides the 8-ounce burger, 8oz sells a 4-ounce option of about 115 grams, which the founders said guests usually finish, while many guests take part of the 8-ounce patty home.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: A founder said he graduated from IBA in 2021, and the restaurant plan began in the months after that graduation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: In the early phase the two founders handled nearly everything themselves, from financing and procurement to running the burger line, with all hands on deck.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said they buy mostly from registered companies on a vendor list of large Pakistani names, and they say they never compromise quality to cut cost.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders told staff to re-cook a dish for an unhappy guest rather than refund it, and gave managers and supervisors full authority to satisfy any guest.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said running a restaurant is a 24-hour job for owners, who stay on board with every decision, so they have to make compromises on family occasions.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said expansion beyond Karachi is under discussion and some offers have come in, but gave no outlet count or timing; they said execution depends on God's will.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: A founder said restaurant openings are loud and visible while closures are quiet, so the restaurant market looks more booming than it is and is a tough, full-time business.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)

fact_text: The founders said restaurant guests bring very different expectations by spend level, and a guest who leaves unsatisfied is hard to win back, unlike a retail product that can be returned.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Building a Burger Brand in Pakistan: The 8oz Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-30)
